critical_code_review_comments: server.py is now 6289 lines — long-standing R21+R22 recommendation to split into routers/, models/, services/ modules still applies (drivers/customer/reviews/dispatch could each be their own router).

driver_cancel_booking is a single ~170-line function doing validation + booking atomic transition + job atomic transition + audit + push + email — the atomic transitions could be wrapped in a MongoDB session/transaction to guarantee all-or-nothing behaviour; today if the jobs.update_one fails right after the bookings.update_one succeeded, the booking is cancelled but the job is still stuck as accepted.
Consider indexing driver_cancellations on {driver_id: 1, created_at: -1} — the /admin/driver-cancellations endpoint sorts by created_at without an index, will slow down at scale.
reviews collection needs unique index on (booking_id, from_id) as backup to the application-layer dedup check to prevent race-window duplicates.
